claims.statement: Domain directories hold portable records and rules for hosts, credentials, connections, sessions, transfers, shell commands, sync and templates rather than live transports or concrete storage, and forbidden imports are checked by ArchitectureBoundaryTests.

Application owns portable use-case and feature state, including broad HostLibraryModel projections, connection journey/trust/retry coordination, and remote-filesystem and repository ports instead of concrete storage and transports.

Application Agent coordinates conversation execution through an injected registry and AgentKit services; Remote Infrastructure Agent registers host resolution, SSH/SFTP, metrics and scratch-transfer capabilities alongside runtime-owned tools.

Persistence owns the versioned SwiftData schema/container and adapters, including scoped sync restrictions, recovery checkpoints, synchronized connection history and the generic device directory. Current V34 migrates released V31 directly, replaces Host/history and Identity shapes and adds workspace preferences; V32 and V33 were never distributed endpoints, and local schema versions do not change CloudKit envelopes. GRDBMemoryStore separately owns a lazily opened SQLite memory database and full-text message index.

Explicit Infrastructure CloudKit coordinators use Persistence journals, scoped safety storage and a shared lifecycle adapter while retaining independent category engines; received and conflicted records share validation, and the SwiftData container disables automatic CloudKit storage.

General Infrastructure separates StoreKit entitlement services, launch-file logging, attachment/skill imports, metrics parsers and Apple speech recognition; speech recognition receives an injected audio-input capability rather than owning app-native capture policy.

Remote Infrastructure SSH owns connection and channel protocol machinery while Transfers owns file-operation scheduling, transfer contexts and edit lifecycles; logical file admission, SSH session-channel admission and physical connection count are distinct controls.
Remote Infrastructure Security implements Keychain and key handling, SSHImport reads/stages concrete import sources, and Telnet is a separate transport rather than a path to SSH-only functionality.

Presentation contains shared forms, formatting, transcript state, SFTP presentation and terminal appearance, while architecture tests prohibit native UI, persistence and remote-infrastructure dependencies in this framework.

Shared resources provide bundle localization, privacy/model metadata and distribution-icon catalogs/assets, while distribution-icon licensing is stored separately and platform-specific icons remain app-owned.

Device metadata is reusable across features: Domain owns DeviceRecord, Application owns DeviceDirectoryModel and its repository port, and Persistence owns the SwiftData repository and Vault journaling adapter independently of connection-history storage.

Xcode file-system-synchronized framework root groups are owned by their corresponding framework targets, while Frameworks/Resources is included by TFM, TFI, TermindWidgets and FrameworkTests rather than by the six shared framework targets; consumers of shared data must not assume it is in their framework bundle.

AssistantExecutionController freezes selected model/secret, permission mode, skills, tool registry and context at submission before optional asynchronous memory and compaction preparation, preventing later UI configuration changes from changing a captured turn.

Application tracks one cancellable agent preparation per conversation, prevents overlapping runs, persists missing-model or missing-credential failures before projecting them to conversation state, and can record interruptions on cancellation; injected AgentRunPersisting keeps SwiftData out of this coordination layer.

The controller composes AgentKit runtime with injected host-tool registry, eligible skill/memory tools, an ordered event channel, and weak conversation approval interaction that denies when closed; compaction is persisted before changing the observable transcript.

SwiftDataAgentRunRepository deduplicates history by message ID across successive run snapshots and stores frozen replay/context backing separately from ordinary messages; it restores transcripts in run order with compaction projection and recovers recorded tool results absent from a later transcript snapshot.

Agent persistence marks unfinished runs interrupted on repository initialization; editing truncates a conversation suffix and stages a replacement user run that a real run later adopts without duplicating the message, while conversation deletion removes its related tool and message backing and tombstones prevent late saves.

RemoteCharsetStreamConverter performs strict outgoing iconv encoding and stateful streaming decoding, buffering incomplete multibyte input while passing malformed received bytes through rather than failing the stream; normal encoding throws on unrepresentable text and optional invalid-input recovery reports rejection.

The remote charset adapter is applied at SSH exec, PTY and SFTP boundaries and also in Telnet; the SSH PTY OSC 7 filter rewrites charset-encoded working-directory paths into percent-encoded UTF-8 for Ghostty, buffering fragmented frames and bounding incomplete payloads.

The presentation icon catalog loads a main-bundle JSON index, resolves detected Linux distribution by exact or like ID and returns no entry if unavailable, while AgentKit searches main/package bundles for the Pi model catalog and optional overrides.

Shared application strings and bundle metadata have separate string catalogs from AgentKit text, and the repository localization check requires completed zh-Hans and zh-Hant translations; Linux distribution assets, catalog and licensing are regenerated together from a pinned Simple Icons version rather than fetched during app use.
